property_summary: For any deployed C, currentVersion() must return the oracle's currentVersion with price transformed by the product payoffDefinition (i.e., equal to C.currentVersion() == payoffDefinition.transform(oracle.currentVersion())), but the mutant returns the raw oracle currentVersion without applying the transform so some oracle prices will differ after transform and break the equality.

For any deployed product C and any oracle address, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant returns the raw oracle currentVersion (no transform), so for some oracle-reported prices the returned .price will differ and the equality breaks.

For any oracle address, C.currentVersion() always returns the oracle's currentVersion with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant returns the raw oracle.currentVersion() (untransformed) so for some oracle-returned prices the price field will differ and the equality will break.

For any oracle-reported price, C.currentVersion() always returns the oracle's currentVersion with its price transformed by the product's payoffDefinition; the mutant returns the raw oracle.currentVersion (untransformed) so there exist oracle prices for which the price field differs and the equality is violated.

For every oracle-reported version, C.currentVersion() returns the oracle's currentVersion with its price transformed by the product payoffDefinition; the mutant returns the raw oracle currentVersion (no transform), so for some oracle-returned prices the .price field differs and the equality is violated.

For any oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoff-transformed price from the underlying oracle; the mutant that returns oracle().atVersion(id) directly will sometimes return an untransformed price and thus differ.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals payoffDefinition.transform(oracle.atVersion(id).price); the mutant that returns oracle().atVersion(id) directly will sometimes return a price not transformed and thus differ.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price field equals the payoffDefinition-transformed price of the underlying oracle's atVersion(id); the mutant that returns oracle().atVersion(id) directly will sometimes return an untransformed price, so there exists an oracleVersion where the returned price differs.

For any oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns an OracleVersion whose price equals the payoffDefinition-transformed price of the underlying oracle's atVersion(id); the mutant that returns oracle().atVersion(id) directly will sometimes return an untransformed price, so there exists an oracleVersion id where the returned price differs.

For every oracleVersion id, C.atVersion(id) returns successfully and the returned OracleVersion.price equals the payoff-transformed underlying oracle price (i.e. calling atVersion does not revert and returns a transformed price); the mutant that returns oracle().atVersion(id) directly will sometimes return an untransformed price causing a mismatch (so the property is violated for some inputs).

For any deployed C, calling maintenance() returns the product's stored maintenance parameter; the mutant that returns controller().minCollateral() will differ when controller().minCollateral() != the stored maintenance value.

For every (fuzzed) storedMaintenance value and a controller minCollateral value, the product's maintenance() getter MUST return the stored maintenance value; the mutant returns controller().minCollateral() instead and thus will differ whenever controller().minCollateral() != stored maintenance (which the fuzzer can find).

For any pair of values (storedMaintenance, controllerMinCollateral) set via product initialization, the correct contract's maintenance() returns the storedMaintenance value; the mutant returns controller().minCollateral() and thus will differ whenever controllerMinCollateral != storedMaintenance.

For any initialized product, maintenance() always returns the product's stored maintenance parameter; the mutant returns controller().minCollateral() instead, so when controller.minCollateral() differs from the stored maintenance the mutant will return a different value.

For any initialized product, C.maintenance() must return the product's stored maintenance parameter; the mutant returns controller().minCollateral() instead, so when controller.minCollateral() != stored maintenance the mutant will produce a different return value.

For all states, makerFee() on the correct contract always returns the stored _makerFee (the committed maker fee) and never a pendingMakerFee; the mutant can return a pendingMakerFee when pending.makerFeeUpdated is set, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For every state, the reference contract's makerFee() always returns the committed stored maker fee (_makerFee); the mutant sometimes returns a pendingMakerFee when pending.makerFeeUpdated is set, so there exist inputs (a pending update applied to pendingFeeUpdates) that make makerFee() return a different value in the mutant.

For all states, the reference contract's makerFee() returns the committed stored maker fee value (the stored _makerFee); the mutant may instead return a pendingMakerFee when a pending maker-fee update exists, so there exist inputs (creating a pending fee update) that make makerFee() return a different value in the mutant.

For every state, the reference contract's makerFee() always returns the committed stored maker fee (_makerFee); the mutant may return a pendingMakerFee when a pending maker-fee update is present, so there exist inputs (creating a pending maker-fee update) that make makerFee() return a different value in the mutant.
